request.user:
[2024 fall ms math-stat — problem 2]

Single observation $Y$ with density $f(y\mid\theta) = (\theta+1)y^\theta$, $0<y<1$. Test $H_0: \theta = 0$ vs $H_a: \theta > 0$ at level $\alpha$. (1) Show a UMP test exists, find it, and give its exact form in terms of $\alpha$. (2) Give its power function in terms of $\alpha$.

response.text:
Let the parameter space be \(\theta>-1\), and test

\[
H_0:\theta=0
\qquad\text{vs.}\qquad
H_a:\theta>0.
\]

The density is

\[
f(y\mid \theta)=(\theta+1)y^\theta,\qquad 0<y<1.
\]

Under \(H_0\), \(\theta=0\), so

\[
f(y\mid 0)=1,\qquad 0<y<1,
\]

i.e. \(Y\sim \mathrm{Unif}(0,1)\).

---

## (1) Existence and form of the UMP level \(\alpha\) test

For any fixed \(\theta_1>0\), consider testing the simple hypotheses

\[
H_0:\theta=0
\qquad\text{vs.}\qquad
H_1:\theta=\theta_1.
\]

The likelihood ratio is

\[
\frac{f(y\mid \theta_1)}{f(y\mid 0)}
=
(\theta_1+1)y^{\theta_1}.
\]

Since \(\theta_1>0\), this is an increasing function of \(y\). Therefore, by the Neyman–Pearson lemma, the most powerful level \(\alpha\) test rejects \(H_0\) for large values of \(Y\).

Because under \(H_0\), \(Y\sim \mathrm{Unif}(0,1)\), we choose \(c_\alpha\) so that

\[
P_0(Y>c_\alpha)=\alpha.
\]

Since \(P_0(Y>c_\alpha)=1-c_\alpha\), we get

\[
1-c_\alpha=\alpha,
\]

so

\[
c_\alpha=1-\alpha.
\]

Thus the level \(\alpha\) test is

\[
\phi_\alpha(y)=
\begin{cases}
1, & y>1-\alpha,\\
0, & y\le 1-\alpha.
\end{cases}
\]

Equivalently, reject \(H_0\) if

\[
Y>1-\alpha.
\]

Because the rejection region does not depend on the particular value \(\theta_1>0\), the same Neyman–Pearson most powerful test works for every simple alternative \(\theta_1>0\). Therefore this test is UMP for testing

\[
H_0:\theta=0
\qquad\text{vs.}\qquad
H_a:\theta>0.
\]

The test has exact size \(\alpha\), since

\[
P_0(Y>1-\alpha)=\alpha.
\]

---

## (2) Power function

For general \(\theta>-1\), the CDF is

\[
F_\theta(y)
=
P_\theta(Y\le y)
=
\int_0^y (\theta+1)t^\theta\,dt
=
y^{\theta+1},
\qquad 0<y<1.
\]

Therefore the power function of the test is

\[
\pi(\theta)
=
P_\theta(Y>1-\alpha)
=
1-F_\theta(1-\alpha).
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\pi(\theta)=1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1}
}
\]

for \(\theta>-1\). In particular, under the null,

\[
\pi(0)=1-(1-\alpha)=\alpha,
\]

so the test has exact level \(\alpha\). For the alternative \(\theta>0\),

\[
\boxed{
\pi(\theta)=1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1},\qquad \theta>0.
}
\]
